column1: # review_specimens/gh_hook.tsv — every post form a review round found, replayed by `review.py specimen-corpus`
# against scrub.gh_hook under a fixture key. A blocker's specimen is a new line here, never only prose.
# expect <TAB> cwd <TAB> command
#   expect  0 = the post passes · 2 = refused
#   cwd     - (the hook's own) · home (the marker-bearing directory below)
#   command \n is a newline; placeholders:
#     {M}      a word the fixture key marks private
#     {HOME}   a directory whose own name carries {M}
#     {CLEAN}  {HOME}/clean.md, a public sentence
#     {DIRTY}  {HOME}/body.md, a line carrying {M}
# #91 build — the first cut

column3: gh issue create --repo o/r --title x --body "measured at {M}"
gh issue create --repo o/r --title x --body "a public sentence"

column1: # #91 round 1 — B1: only what travels is scrubbed (a path, a cd, a --repo never reach GitHub)

column3: cd {HOME} && gh issue close 91 --repo o/r --comment done

column1: # #91 round 1 — B2: a body the hook cannot read refuses

column3: cd {HOME} && gh issue create --title t -F body.md
gh issue create --title t --body-file - <<'EOF'\na public sentence\nEOF

python3 - <<'PY'
sp = '{HOME}'
print("gh issue comment 1 --body x")
PY
gh issue close 3 --comment done

gh issue comment 9 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
1) the first
2) a :) face
EOF
)"

column1: # #91 round 2 — B3: a post is recognised from parsed words, however gh is named and wherever its flags sit
# #91 round 2 — B4: a word the shell builds is read when static, refused otherwise

column3: cat notes | xargs gh issue comment 1 -b
gh issue create --title t --body '## What\n`scrub.py` costs $5 and '"'"'$(nothing)'"'"' runs'
gh issue create --title t --body '## What\n`scrub.py` is for {M}'

column1: # #91 round 3 — B5: every word after the head travels (no flag arity assumed); B6: expansions; B7: verbs and shells
# #91 round 4 — B9: a heredoc spelled inside quotes is text, and a heredoc fed to a shell is a script
# #91 round 4 — B10: a quoted word is never a redirection
# #91 round 4 — B11: a built word in the group or verb slot expands or refuses
# #91 round 5 — B12: a shell's script (options before -c, a prefix assignment, a built -c/eval) · B13: bash's heredoc end line and delimiter · B14: a greedy quoted-heredoc body

column3:
gh issue create --repo o/r --label x --title "a (t) title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What
`scrub.py` costs $5, <<EOF and a > b (really) $(nothing) 1) item
EOF
)"

column1: # #91 round 6 — B15: an assignment bash keeps (or drops) where the hook read otherwise

column3: B=a; if true; then B="$(cat {DIRTY})"; fi; gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"
B=a; export B={M}; gh issue comment 1 -b "$B"
B=a; for x in 1; do B={M}; done; gh issue comment 1 -b "$B"
B={M}; B=a true; gh issue comment 1 -b "$B"

column1: # #91 round 6 — B16: a file written earlier in the same command is posted as bash leaves it

column3: echo {M} | tee clean.md >/dev/null; gh issue comment 1 --body-file clean.md

cat > {CLEAN} <<'EOF'
a public sentence
EOF
gh issue create --title t --body-file {CLEAN}

column1: # #91 round 7 — B17: `new` is gh's own alias of create, and a repo's description travels
# #91 round 7 — B18: an assignment bash may skip (`||` · `&&`) or run in a subshell (`|` · `&`) is not the value bash keeps

column3: B={M}; true || B=clean; gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"
B="$(cat {DIRTY})"; test -s {DIRTY} || B="a public sentence"; gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"
B={M}; false && B=clean; gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"
B={M}; B=clean | cat; gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"
B={M}; case y in x) true; B=clean;; esac; gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"
true && B="a public sentence" && gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"

column1: # #91 round 7 — B19: a closed block returns the depth to 0, so a clean filing after a loop or a branch passes

column3: for f in a b; do echo $f; done; B="a public sentence"; gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"
if true; then echo ok; fi\nB="a public sentence"\ngh issue comment 1 --body "$B"
while false; do :; done; B="a public sentence"; gh issue comment 1 --body "$B"

column1: # #91 round 8 — a branch name, a project item and a run's inputs travel; gh's own output redirected to a file is a write the hook cannot read

column3: gh issue view 1 > {CLEAN}; gh issue comment 1 -F {CLEAN}

column1: # #91 round 8 (B20) — a `cd` inside `( … )` ends with the subshell; `cd -`, `pushd` and `popd` are followed, never read as directories

column3: ( cd .. && true ) && gh issue comment 1 --body-file clean.md
cd .. && cd - >/dev/null && gh issue comment 1 --body-file clean.md
cd .. ; cd -; gh issue comment 1 --body-file body.md
pushd .. >/dev/null && popd >/dev/null && gh issue comment 1 --body-file clean.md
cd .. && cd - >/dev/null && gh issue comment 1 --body-file body.md

column1: # #91 round 9 — B21: `>&` · `<&` · `&>` are one redirection word, never split at the `&`

column3: git status > log.txt 2>&1; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
echo warn >&2; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
ls 2>&1 | tail -1; gh issue comment 1 --body "$(cat clean.md)"
echo {M} &> clean.md; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
echo {M} >& clean.md; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
echo {M} > clean.md 2>&1; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md

column1: # #91 round 9 — B22: `workflow run` is recognised by its words, wherever the flags sit, and `--json` reads its inputs from stdin

column3: gh workflow --repo o/r run x.yml -f note={M}

column1: # #91 round 10 — B23: a post standing inside `$(…)` or a backtick is a command, walked like a script (the `sh -c` · `eval` class)

column3: URL="$(gh issue create --repo o/r --title t --body {M})"; echo "$URL"
N=$(gh pr create -t t -b {M} | tail -1); echo $N
if [ -n "$(gh issue comment 1 -b {M})" ]; then echo ok; fi
URL=$(gh issue create -t t -b "a public sentence"); echo "$URL"
S={HOME}; URL=$(gh issue create -t t -F $S/body.md); echo "$URL"
S={HOME}; URL=$(gh issue create -t t -F $S/clean.md); echo "$URL"

column1: # #91 round 11 — B24: a posted word is scrubbed whole; the text after its first `=` is never re-expanded as live shell

column3:
gh issue comment 1 -b "$(cat <<'EOF'
the idiom: URL=$(gh issue create -t t -b x)
EOF
)"

column1: # #91 round 11 — B25: a writer inside a walked `$(…)` or `eval` marks the outer command; the depth cap refuses, never skips

column3:
cat > gen.py <<'EOF'
open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')
EOF
x=$(python3 gen.py); gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
x=$(bash -c "echo {M} > clean.md"); gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
eval "cp body.md clean.md"; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md

column1: # #91 round 12 — B26: a writer after `do` · `then` · `else` · `time` · `env` · `!` · `{` or in a function body is a writer; B27: a child shell's walk sees the outer's writes

column3: for n in 1; do python3 -c "open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')"; done; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
time python3 -c "open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')"; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
env X=1 python3 -c "open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')"; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
if true; then cp body.md clean.md; fi; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
true && { cp body.md clean.md; } && gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
f() { cp body.md clean.md; }; f; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
for n in 1; do python3 -c "open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')"; done; gh issue comment 1 --body "$(cat clean.md)"
for n in 1; do echo $n; done; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
time ls >/dev/null; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
if true; then echo ok; fi; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
echo {M} > clean.md; bash -c 'gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md'
echo {M} > clean.md; bash <<'EOF'\ngh issue comment 1 -F clean.md\nEOF
cp body.md clean.md; sh -c 'gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md'

column1: # #91 round 13 — B28: a redirect heading a segment (after `( … )`, or before the command word) is a write; B29: a writer after `if` · `while` · `until` · `function` is a writer; a prefix word's separated flag value is not the command

column3: ( echo {M} ) > clean.md; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
( cd .. && echo {M} ) > clean.md 2>&1; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
( echo {M} ) >> clean.md; gh issue comment 1 --body "$(cat clean.md)"
( echo {M} ) &> clean.md; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
( echo {M} ) > clean.md && gh issue comment 1 --body-file clean.md
x=$( ( echo {M} ) > clean.md ); gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
> clean.md echo {M}; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
( echo ok ) > log.txt; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
if python3 -c "open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')"; then gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md; fi
if cp body.md clean.md; then gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md; fi
if cp body.md clean.md\nthen gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md\nfi
if ! cp body.md clean.md; then echo no; fi; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
while ! cp body.md clean.md; do sleep 1; done; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
until cp body.md clean.md; do break; done; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
function f { cp body.md clean.md; }; f; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
if [ -f body.md ]; then gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md; fi
if grep -q public clean.md; then gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md; fi
nice -n 5 python3 -c "open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')"; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
env -u X python3 -c "open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')"; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md

column1: # #91 round 14 — B30: a prefix word's value flags are its own (`time -p` and `command -p` take none; `command -v X` names X, never runs it); `< F` heads a segment like `> F`

column3: time -p cp body.md clean.md; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
time -p python3 -c "open('clean.md','w').write('{M}')"; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
command -p cp body.md clean.md; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
< body.md tee clean.md >/dev/null; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
< body.md python3 -c "import sys; open('clean.md','w').write(sys.stdin.read())"; gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
command -v python3 >/dev/null && gh issue comment 1 -F clean.md
